title: Terraform custom and predefined URL category resources
aliases: delete url category still in use terraform

prose.text: Terraform manages custom categories with `zia_url_categories` and edits predefined ones with `zia_url_categories_predefined`. {{import-custom-only}} {{predefined-import-only}}

prose.label: Predefined categories.
prose.text: It is one of the Early Access resources listed in [[zia.terraform.early-access:early-access-resources]]. {{predefined-incremental}} {{predefined-description-drift}} {{predefined-import-captures-existing}}

checks.do: Whether a DLP rule references the category by `val` rather than by name.
Whether an import of a predefined category lists every custom item the HCL should keep before the next apply.
Which custom category cap applies to the tenant, since the provider docs and the help page differ.

url-order-diff-suppressed.statement: Provider v4.7.23 fixed `zia_url_categories` planning failing after import, or whenever the API returned `urls` in a different order from the HCL, and re-ordering URLs in the configuration produces no diff.

quotes: Fixed a regression in the `zia_url_categories` resource where `terraform plan` could fail immediately after `terraform import` (or any time the API returned the `urls` list in a different order than the one declared in HCL)
re-ordering URLs in the configuration continues to produce no diff

val-for-dlp-reference.statement: The numeric `val` attribute is the category's unique ID and the one to use when referencing the category in other resources such as DLP web rules.

quotes: * `val` - (Number) The unique ID for the URL category. This attribute is particularly useful when referencing the URL category in other resources like DLP web rules.

tf-limit-48-custom.statement: The provider documentation says up to 48 custom URL categories can be added per organization.

quotes: Up to 48 custom URL categories can be added per organization.

import-custom-only.statement: `zia_url_categories` imports only custom categories, by category ID or name; built-in categories cannot be imported.

quotes: This provider only supports the importing of custom URL categories. The importing of built-in categories is not supported.
**zia_url_categories** can be imported by using `<CATEGORY_ID>` or `<CATEGORY_NAME>` as the import ID.

delete-detaches-v4-7-26.statement: From provider v4.7.26 deleting a custom URL category first detaches it from every rule that references it, avoiding the API error for a category still in use.

quotes: The `zia_url_categories` resource now automatically detaches a custom URL category from any rules that reference it before deleting the category. This removes the need to manually remove the category from rules first and avoids the API error returned when deleting a category that is still in use.

predefined-incremental.statement: `zia_url_categories_predefined` changes predefined categories with incremental `ADD_TO_LIST` and `REMOVE_FROM_LIST` operations for its list fields rather than replacing the category.

quotes: The provider uses incremental `ADD_TO_LIST` and `REMOVE_FROM_LIST` API operations for all list fields

predefined-description-drift.statement: The `description` attribute is not supported on predefined categories because the API accepts it in the PUT but does not return it in the GET, which would cause persistent drift.

quotes: The `description` attribute is **not** supported by this resource. Although the API accepts a description in the PUT payload, the value is not returned in the GET response for predefined categories, which would cause persistent state drift.

predefined-import-captures-existing.statement: Importing a predefined category that already has custom URLs, keywords or IP ranges captures them in state, and the next apply attempts to remove any that the HCL omits.

quotes: When importing a predefined category that already has custom URLs, keywords, or IP ranges configured (e.g., via the ZIA Admin Portal), those existing items will be captured in the Terraform state.
If your HCL configuration does not include those items, the **next** `terraform apply` will attempt to **remove** them to match the desired state defined in your configuration.

predefined-import-only.statement: `zia_url_categories_predefined` imports only predefined categories, by category ID or display name; custom categories use `zia_url_categories`.

quotes: Predefined URL categories can be imported by using the predefined category ID or display name as the import ID.
This resource only supports importing **predefined** URL categories. For custom URL categories, use the [`zia_url_categories`](zia_url_categories) resource.

issue-615-remove-clears-other-lists.statement: Provider issue #615, still open, reports against v4.8.13 that removing a URL from `urls` on `zia_url_categories` also removes the desired `db_categorized_urls` entries from the category in ZIA even when `db_categorized_urls` is unchanged in configuration, that planned changes to `db_categorized_urls` are then not applied, and that the next plan shows drift. The reporter's explanation is that ZIA applies the action to every list in the payload.

quotes: terraform-provider-zia: **v4.8.13**
also removes the desired `db_categorized_urls` entries from the category, even when `db_categorized_urls` is unchanged in config.
Planned changes to `db_categorized_urls` are not applied: removals never happen
The plan doesn't show any of this.
ZIA applies the action to every list in the payload, not just `urls`.
When `urls` changes on an existing `zia_url_categories` resource, Update sends only incremental
After the apply, Read refreshes state from the API, and the **next** plan shows drift.

issue-575-large-category-refresh.statement: Provider issue #575 reported that a custom URL category of about 19,000 `urls` entries took 15 to 20 minutes per plan on v4.7.18 while the same data came back from the ZIA REST endpoint in about 5 seconds. A repository member replied that v4.7.22 cut a 20,000 URL fresh create from several minutes to about 35 seconds and a refresh from many minutes to about 20 seconds. These figures are the reporter's and the vendor's.

quotes: `terraform plan` refresh of a single `zia_url_categories` resource holding ~19,000 entries in `urls` takes 15–20 minutes per run.
The same data via the underlying ZIA REST endpoint returns in ~5 seconds.
Fresh create: several minutes → ~35 seconds. Refresh: many minutes → ~20 seconds.
I tested v4.7.23 and looks like we're good. 17 URL cats, code over 20k lines and plan passed after 1m and 6 seconds.
+ provider registry.terraform.io/zscaler/zia v4.7.18
Please upgrade to v4.7.22 and rerun your plan.

custom-category-cap-48-vs-64.summary: How many custom URL categories a tenant can hold by default.

positions.says: The Terraform resource documentation says up to 48 custom URL categories per organization.

quotes: Up to 48 custom URL categories can be added per organization.

positions.says: The Ranges and Limitations help page gives 64 as the default limit for custom categories.

quotes: The default limit for custom categories is 64.

custom-category-cap-48-vs-64.impact: Do not quote 48 as the tenant limit from the provider docs alone; the help page figure is 64, raisable through Support, and which is current for a given tenant is not settled here.

large-category-plan-time.title: How long a plan or refresh takes for a custom category with tens of thousands of URLs
large-category-plan-time.blocks: saying that planning a large custom URL category is slow or fast
large-category-plan-time.detail: Upstream issue 575 reports the plan time of a roughly 20,000 URL category before and after the v4.7.22 fix (issue-575-large-category-refresh); those are third-party figures. A plan time measured on a category of that size, with the vendored provider, is still open.

issue-615-reproduction.title: Whether ZIA applies REMOVE_FROM_LIST to the other lists in the payload
issue-615-reproduction.blocks: saying that a URL removal on a custom category keeps its db_categorized_urls entries
issue-615-reproduction.detail: Issue 615 states that ZIA applies the action to every list in the payload; the vendored provider source builds the incremental payloads from the whole desired category with only `urls` replaced (custom-category-remove-then-add), so the request shape matches the report, but the service behavior was not reproduced. Remove a URL from `urls` on a category that holds `db_categorized_urls` entries and read the category back.
